minor: 'Researchers from the University of San Francisco had already run a randomized trial' sits in the 2014 section, but the El Salvador findings were published in 2018 (the shoe-seller paper in 2014). Say 'would later publish' or 'were running' so viewers don't think the health result was known at the time of the deal.
'Researchers found children wore them, and liked them, in El Salvador' is accurate to the study but has no entry in `sources`. Add one, or soften it.

'So did rivals: Skechers launched BOBS in 2010' follows the 2011 eyewear and book lines. This reads as if rivals copied after 2011, when BOBS actually came first. 'Canvas lookalike' is also a descriptor the sources don't give.
'Customers didn't, because they never knew' is an inference, not a documented fact. 'Cheaper lookalikes filled big-box shelves, many with no pledge at all' is also unsourced detail.
The shot labelled (quote) 'The promise had a name that would become a slogan...' contains no quotation and never names the promise.

'The giving grew faster than anyone planned, and the company counted every pair out loud' has no source and no figure. The sourced 1 millionth (2010) and 10 millionth (2013) pair milestones would make it concrete.
'The money from the 2014 deal went to the founder' is a simplification. The source says only that the founder kept half and pledged half of his proceeds.
